name: US Citizenship Naturalization Civics Test
description: Study knowledge base for the official USCIS naturalization civics test covering American government, U.S. history, and integrated civics with short oral answers, including 2008 100-question and 2025 128-question versions.

concepts.label: Congress and Legislative Branch
concepts.description: Senate and House, terms, numbers, representation, powers and current members.

concepts.label: 1900s and Modern History
concepts.description: World Wars, Great Depression, civil rights movement, recent wars and modern presidents.

concepts.label: Presidency and Executive Branch
concepts.description: President, Vice President, succession, Cabinet, powers and current officeholders.

concepts.label: Colonial Period and Independence
concepts.description: Colonies, founders, Revolution, Constitution Convention and early nation documents.

concepts.label: Geography and Levels of Government
concepts.description: States, capitals, territories, federal vs state powers, governors and local government.

concepts.label: Constitution and Bill of Rights
concepts.description: Amendments, Bill of Rights, First Amendment freedoms and other constitutional protections.

concepts.label: Rights and Responsibilities of Citizens
concepts.description: Citizen rights, duties, oath, pledge, participation and service to the nation.

concepts.label: Courts and Judicial Branch
concepts.description: Supreme Court, judicial review, justices, Chief Justice and court functions.

concepts.label: Elections and Voting
concepts.description: Voting rights, elections timing, political parties, Speaker and state and federal officials.

concepts.label: 1800s and Civil War History
concepts.description: Territorial expansion, Civil War, slavery, Lincoln, amendments 13-15 and industrial era.

concepts.label: National Symbols and Holidays
concepts.description: Flag, anthem, monuments, federal holidays and meaning of national symbols.

concepts.label: Declaration of Independence
concepts.description: Independence from Great Britain, life liberty pursuit of happiness and founding documents.

concepts.label: Principles of American Democracy
concepts.description: Supreme law, self-government, rule of law, Constitution purpose, market economy and founding ideals.

concepts.label: Separation of Powers
concepts.description: Three branches, checks and balances and prevention of concentrated power.

levels.descriptor: Perfect score; all 20 questions answered correctly.
Passing for 2025 test; 12 correct answers stops the test as passed.
Below passing; one more incorrect answer (9 incorrect) results in failure.
No correct answers; does not demonstrate required civics knowledge.

dimensions.label: Civics Accuracy
dimensions.ask: Did the response give an accepted USCIS answer for history and government?

dimensions.label: Currency of Officeholders
dimensions.ask: For changeable answers, is the official serving at interview time named?

dimensions.label: Oral Completeness
dimensions.ask: Is the short oral answer complete and intelligible without extra incorrect content?

dimensions.label: Test Procedure Knowledge
dimensions.ask: Does preparation reflect up-to-10-question 2008 or 20-question 2025 oral rules and 65/20 special consideration?

rubric.notes: 2008 test: officer asks up to 10 of 100 questions, pass with 6 correct, fail with 5 incorrect. 2025 test based on 2020 128 questions: officer asks 20 questions, pass with 12 correct, fail with 9 incorrect, stopping early when threshold reached. Age 65+ with 20+ years as LPR studies 20 starred questions and takes test in language of choice. For senators, representative, president, vice president, chief justice, speaker, governor and party, answer with officeholder serving at interview; USCIS accepts listed variants.
